## Item (a) — the identity notion for attestation reuse — is SETTLED by operator ruling

Recording only the settled item; the rest of this ADR is untouched.

The operator ruled, verbatim:

> "Certification environment should not currently be a gate. Any certification is as good as any
> other certification right now. Limited to a trusted set of environments is a future feature, but
> not currently in use."

### What this settles for item (a)

The identity scope for attestation reuse is **not** the signing environment/principal. Reuse is
scoped by the *validity of the signature* and the attestation's own material/staleness pins — not
by which environment minted it. Concretely:

- A plan-review or completion-verifier op-cert signed in environment A is reusable in environment
  B, provided the envelope itself verifies. Cross-environment identity alone is never a refusal.
- What still refuses: an envelope that does not verify (`mismatch`), or none at all (`unsigned`).
  Loosening identity does not loosen cryptographic verification.
- The trusted-set restriction (`verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since`,
  `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`) is retained as a **future, opt-in** feature. It must not
  gate while unset, and must behave exactly as today when an operator sets it.

This is consistent with — and now generalizes — the operator's earlier ruling on bug
`stuffed-custommade-nuthatch` (846b) for the bugfix-size gate: gate on the FACT of certification,
never on its SOURCE.

Implementation of the settled ruling is tracked on bug `loathful-unanarchic-chickadee`
(`c21f-6f29-5d2d-4a5a`), which corrects both the code path
(`_opcert_signing.verify_opcert_record`) and the docs that encoded the future restriction as live
policy.

Items other than (a) remain open.
